To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the synchronization of an IoT device with a blockchain network is a communication-intensive operation that requires careful consideration of the trade-off between the communication cost and the security level of the protocol, and that the power consumption of the IoT device can be reduced at the expense of a longer synchronization time.
the synchronization protocols that are most suitable for IoT devices are the lightest ones, which require the lowest communication overhead and power consumption.
the synchronization traffic generated by a blockchain network depends on the synchronization protocol, and it is significantly higher than the traffic generated by a centralized database.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: 1) What are the synchronization requirements for blockchain-based IoT systems?
the following questions: How does the communication traffic generated by blockchain synchronization protocols scale with the network size and the number of transactions?

the following aspects of the blockchain synchronization problem: (a) modeling the communication traffic generated by the blockchain synchronization protocols, (b) modeling the power consumption of an IoT device during the synchronization, and (c) investigating the trade-offs between the communication and the power consumption of the IoT device.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the communication traffic generated by the blockchain synchronization of IoT devices is proportional to the size of the blockchain and inversely proportional to the bandwidth of the communication channel.
the synchronization traffic generated by a device is proportional to the number of transactions it observes, while its power consumption is proportional to the size of the blockchain.
, in a blockchain-powered IoT system, the synchronization traffic is a major bottleneck, and the synchronization protocols must be optimized to minimize the synchronization traffic.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the communication cost and synchronization delay for the blockchain synchronization protocols are inversely proportional to the number of IoT devices connected to the blockchain.

we provide a rigorous analysis of blockchain synchronization in the IoT ecosystem, with a particular focus on the communication traffic generated by the IoT devices, as well as the power consumption and the synchronization trade-off.

we provide a framework to analyze the trade-off between the communication cost and the security level of a blockchain synchronization protocol, and to quantify the energy efficiency of such protocols.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the communication overhead for synchronization can be significantly reduced by using an efficient synchronization protocol and by exploiting the sporadic nature of IoT devices, which are often in idle mode.
a blockchain synchronization protocol that is designed to reduce the communication traffic between an IoT device and its validator nodes can significantly reduce the power consumption of the device.
a careful design of the blockchain synchronization protocols and the communication stack can reduce the power consumption of the IoT devices, with a small performance degradation.
